requirements.text: The institution draws up a systematic integrity risk analysis (SIRA) of its inherent ML/TF risks, performs it periodically according to a predetermined protocol, records the results in writing and adapts it to internal and external developments.
requirements.level_reason: The systematic integrity risk analysis is an institution-wide assessment evidenced in the SIRA, not in model documentation.
requirements.verification_note: Paraphrased; checked against the English DNB Guideline on the Wwft and Sw (edition reflecting legal text of Aug 2019), §3.2/3.3, p. 12-13, 15. DNB reportedly replaced this Guideline in May 2024 with its Wwft Q&As and Good Practices; confirm the current source.

requirements.text: The SIRA covers risk identification, risk analysis of likelihood and impact, design of risk controls, and risk monitoring including review of the analysis.
requirements.level_reason: The content of the systematic integrity risk analysis is evidenced in the SIRA, not in model documentation.
requirements.verification_note: Paraphrased; checked against the English DNB Guideline on the Wwft and Sw (edition reflecting legal text of Aug 2019), §3.2, p. 13-14. DNB reportedly replaced this Guideline in May 2024 with its Wwft Q&As and Good Practices; confirm the current source.

requirements.text: Risk identification in the SIRA is based on risk factors relating to customers, services, products, transactions, delivery channels and countries or geography, with the institution assessing the likelihood and impact of each risk.
requirements.level_reason: Risk identification within the systematic integrity risk analysis is evidenced in the SIRA, not in model documentation.
requirements.verification_note: Paraphrased; checked against the English DNB Guideline on the Wwft and Sw (edition reflecting legal text of Aug 2019), §3.3, p. 13-15. DNB reportedly replaced this Guideline in May 2024 with its Wwft Q&As and Good Practices; confirm the current source.

requirements.text: The institution classifies its entire customer base into risk categories based on objective, identifiable factors, taking into account all risk factors that could affect the integrity risk of the relationship.
requirements.verification_note: Paraphrased; checked against the English DNB Guideline on the Wwft and Sw (edition reflecting legal text of Aug 2019), §3.1/3.4, p. 12, 17. DNB reportedly replaced this Guideline in May 2024 with its Wwft Q&As and Good Practices; confirm the current source.

requirements.text: The customer classification system is documented in writing, for example in the customer acceptance policy, with a number of risk categories consistent with the nature, size and complexity of the institution's risk factors.
requirements.verification_note: Paraphrased; checked against the English DNB Guideline on the Wwft and Sw (edition reflecting legal text of Aug 2019), §3.4, p. 17. DNB reportedly replaced this Guideline in May 2024 with its Wwft Q&As and Good Practices; confirm the current source.

requirements.text: The frequency of periodic customer file reviews is determined by the customer's risk category.
requirements.verification_note: Paraphrased; checked against the English DNB Guideline on the Wwft and Sw (edition reflecting legal text of Aug 2019), §3.4, p. 17, 19. DNB reportedly replaced this Guideline in May 2024 with its Wwft Q&As and Good Practices; confirm the current source. The Guideline gives illustrative review frequencies per category (e.g. three to five years for low risk).

requirements.text: The institution defines the circumstances triggering an event-driven customer file review and, if it relies on event-driven reviews only, can demonstrate that the triggering scenarios are sufficiently effective.
requirements.verification_note: Paraphrased; checked against the English DNB Guideline on the Wwft and Sw (edition reflecting legal text of Aug 2019), §3.4, p. 17. DNB reportedly replaced this Guideline in May 2024 with its Wwft Q&As and Good Practices; confirm the current source.

requirements.text: In addition to the risk category, the institution draws up an individual customer risk profile based on the relevant risk factors and uses it to monitor the business relationship.
requirements.verification_note: Paraphrased; checked against the English DNB Guideline on the Wwft and Sw (edition reflecting legal text of Aug 2019), §3.4, p. 17. DNB reportedly replaced this Guideline in May 2024 with its Wwft Q&As and Good Practices; confirm the current source.

requirements.text: The transaction monitoring process reflects the ML/TF risks identified in the SIRA, which forms the basis for transaction monitoring policy, processes and procedures.
requirements.verification_note: Paraphrased; checked against the English DNB Guideline on the Wwft and Sw (edition reflecting legal text of Aug 2019), §5.1, p. 50-51. DNB reportedly replaced this Guideline in May 2024 with its Wwft Q&As and Good Practices; confirm the current source.

requirements.text: The institution prepares an expected transaction profile per customer or customer peer group and uses it to assess whether conducted transactions are consistent with its knowledge of the customer.
requirements.verification_note: Paraphrased; checked against the English DNB Guideline on the Wwft and Sw (edition reflecting legal text of Aug 2019), §5.1, p. 50-51. DNB reportedly replaced this Guideline in May 2024 with its Wwft Q&As and Good Practices; confirm the current source.

requirements.text: The institution operates an automated transaction monitoring system, where transaction volumes warrant it, with a substantiated and adequate set of business rules consisting of detection scenarios and threshold values.
requirements.verification_note: Paraphrased; checked against the English DNB Guideline on the Wwft and Sw (edition reflecting legal text of Aug 2019), §5.1/5.2, p. 51-52. DNB reportedly replaced this Guideline in May 2024 with its Wwft Q&As and Good Practices; confirm the current source.

requirements.text: The institution periodically tests its transaction monitoring business rules on both technical functioning and effectiveness.
requirements.verification_note: Paraphrased; checked against the English DNB Guideline on the Wwft and Sw (edition reflecting legal text of Aug 2019), §5.1, p. 51. DNB reportedly replaced this Guideline in May 2024 with its Wwft Q&As and Good Practices; confirm the current source.

requirements.article: DNB Leidraad Wwft/Sw §5.1 (Good Practices transaction monitoring)
requirements.text: Threshold calibration is supported by above-the-line and below-the-line testing, analysing alert outcomes above and samples of non-alerted activity below the thresholds to substantiate threshold settings.
requirements.verification_note: The Guideline (§5.1, p. 51) requires periodic testing of business rules for effectiveness but does not itself mention ATL/BTL testing. ATL/BTL is described in DNB's Good Practices on post-event transaction monitoring (2017) and the 2024 Wwft Q&As and Good Practices; exact location not verified.

requirements.text: Alert investigation findings are recorded adequately and clearly, including the considerations and conclusions underlying each decision to close or escalate an alert and whether or not to report.
requirements.level_reason: Recording of alert investigation findings is evidenced in the case management system and investigation procedures.
requirements.verification_note: Paraphrased; checked against the English DNB Guideline on the Wwft and Sw (edition reflecting legal text of Aug 2019), §5.1/5.2, p. 51-52. DNB reportedly replaced this Guideline in May 2024 with its Wwft Q&As and Good Practices; confirm the current source.

requirements.text: Transaction monitoring governance provides clear segregation of duties, for example through the three lines of defence model.
requirements.level_reason: Segregation of duties in transaction monitoring governance is evidenced in the institution's three lines of defence organisation.
requirements.verification_note: Paraphrased; checked against the English DNB Guideline on the Wwft and Sw (edition reflecting legal text of Aug 2019), §5.1, p. 51. DNB reportedly replaced this Guideline in May 2024 with its Wwft Q&As and Good Practices; confirm the current source.

requirements.text: Before monitoring, the institution ensures that all relevant customer, service and transaction data are fully and accurately included in the transaction monitoring process.
requirements.verification_note: Paraphrased; checked against the English DNB Guideline on the Wwft and Sw (edition reflecting legal text of Aug 2019), §5.2, p. 52. DNB reportedly replaced this Guideline in May 2024 with its Wwft Q&As and Good Practices; confirm the current source.

requirements.text: The quality and effectiveness of the transaction monitoring system is demonstrable, for example through a model validation or audit.
requirements.verification_note: Paraphrased; checked against the English DNB Guideline on the Wwft and Sw (edition reflecting legal text of Aug 2019), §5.2, p. 52. DNB reportedly replaced this Guideline in May 2024 with its Wwft Q&As and Good Practices; confirm the current source.

requirements.text: The institution has sufficient in-house understanding of its monitoring systems, including advanced or AI-based systems, and does not rely on algorithms provided by external suppliers.
requirements.verification_note: Paraphrased; checked against the English DNB Guideline on the Wwft and Sw (edition reflecting legal text of Aug 2019), §5.2, p. 52. DNB reportedly replaced this Guideline in May 2024 with its Wwft Q&As and Good Practices; confirm the current source.
